external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: Deployed sensor nodes installed on customer sites and outside the system operator's physical control.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites. They are outside our physical control
external_entities.notes: The authentication key is per fleet, not per device, and has not been rotated since deployment.

external_entities.name: technician
external_entities.description: Field technician servicing sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: a technician can be standing next to one with a laptop
external_entities.notes: The authentication provided by the local serial console is unknown.

external_entities.name: laptop
external_entities.description: Laptop that may be used by a technician near a sensor node.
external_entities.source_excerpt: a technician can be standing next to one with a laptop

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: Operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: Internet-exposed MQTT broker that authenticates sensor nodes and forwards accepted readings.
processes.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE
processes.notes: Nodes authenticate with a fleet-wide pre-shared key that has not been rotated since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: Python consumer that picks up readings from Pub/Sub and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboards
processes.description: Dashboards used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: Firestore registry used to check a device key and determine which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: Pub/Sub service carrying readings from the device gateway to the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: BigQuery telemetry store containing site addresses and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the telemetry lake in BigQuery. The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes retrieve firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image and install what they find. The bucket is public read
data_stores.notes: It is unknown whether nodes check a signature on the image before installing it.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes publish readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up the device in the device registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes poll the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: service console
data_flows.description: Field technicians service sensor nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The authentication provided by the console is unknown.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: Fleet operators view dashboards over BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer site
trust_boundaries.description: Customer site where deployed sensor nodes are installed and outside the system operator's physical control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: GKE
trust_boundaries.description: GKE environment where the device gateway MQTT broker runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: an MQTT broker we run on GKE

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: Network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential because it contains authentication keys and customer associations.
assumptions.basis: The description says the registry is used to check the key and determine which customer the node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is confidential because it carries sensor readings that are customer data.
assumptions.basis: The gateway forwards accepted readings to Pub/Sub, and the telemetry lake is explicitly described as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The description explicitly states that the lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns and is customer data.
